A tak my take giz vplnie z praweny gsucze a k tomu take s dobru a plnu wuoly stran obu swrchupsanych mezy nymi wypowiediely gsme a moczy listu tohoto k wiecznemu drzenij wypowiedame takto: Nayprwe ze tu' czestu, kteraz gest od staradawna ze wsy kamene na gich pole a do gich lesuow, tu magij lydee z te wsy swobodnu gmiety bez prziekazy Ludwikowy y geho buduczych. Item potok, kteryz tecze mymo wet gessto slowe kamenna, ten ma knyez opat a con- went swrchupsanij y gich buduczy drzety a toho pozywaty az po ty hranycze , yakoz gsu vsazeny kamen s krzyzem s gedne strany potoka a z druhe strany podstranij ynhed proly tomu take kamen s krzyzem a od toho kamene doluow az do Zumberka, ten potok ma Ludwik nadepsany a geho buduczy drzety a toho pozywati bez prziekazy opatowy a conwcnta swrchupsanych y gich buduczych. Item o zagezek w tom klassterskem potocze wypowiedam^e, aby geig sobie Ludwik a geho buduczy swym nakladem op¡-a\vowaly tak, aby gym woda do rybnyka ssla, ale toho zagezku nema powyssowati any wyss dielaty nez yako nynie znamenano gest. Item o zakop mezy lukamy a pastwami Ludwikowymi a mezy diedynami tiech lidij kla- ssterskych wypowiedame, aby ten oprawowaly takto lidee klasster- sstij z kainenne gedno leto, kdyz by se pokazyl a druhe leto Ludwik u geho buduczy a tak wdyczky po wsseczka leta, kdyz by toho potrzebie bylo v buduczych czasiech oprawowaty magij. Tuto nassy wypowied slybili gsu obie stranie swrchupsane od sebe y swych buduczych sobie wiernie a prawie drzety a zachowaty bez przeru- ssenie wsselikeho. A tobo na swiedomye peczet nassy wietssy s nassy wuoly a gistym wiedomym przywiesyti gsme kazaly k tomuto listu. Genz gest dan a psan na Crumlowie leta po- narozenij syna bozieho tisycz cztrzsteho ssedesateho prteho w to nediely den swateho Mauriezij. entries.english:
1465 September 22. Krumau. — Johann von Rosenberg amicably settles the dispute between Hohenfurt Monastery and Ludwig von Sonnberg concerning a shared road, a field, and a stream near Sacheries.

CCXLVII. I, Jan von Rosenberg, make known publicly by this letter before all who see it or hear it read that a dispute had arisen between our dear spiritual friends, the abbot and convent of Hohenfurt Monastery on one side and the renowned Ludwig von Sonnberg on the other, concerning a stream, a road, and boundaries, which are set out below. Since both parties had fully submitted these matters to our authority, we sent our councillors Jan of Petrowitz, then burgrave at Krumau, and Girzijek of Wietrznie to inspect and examine them. The parties named above also appointed the following good men to assist in the inspection: Girzijek Grossawer, Przibik Zybrzid of Mostek, Oldrzych of Dworcze, then burgrave of Nové Hrady, Erasim of Michnicz, and Woytiech of Giwowicz. They all carefully and clearly inspected all these matters and reported them to us fully and intelligibly, so that we understood them as if we had been there in person. Therefore, having now been fully informed, and with the full and willing consent of both parties named above, we have declared between them, and by the authority of this letter declare for perpetual observance, as follows: First, the road that from ancient times runs from the village of Kamenná to their fields and forests may be used freely by the people of that village, without hindrance from Ludwig or his successors. As for the stream that flows past the farmstead called Kamenná, the aforesaid abbot and convent and their successors shall hold and use it up to the boundaries marked by a stone set with a cross on one side of the stream, and another stone with a cross on the other side, below the slope directly opposite; from that stone downstream to Sonnberg, the aforesaid Ludwig and his successors shall hold and use the stream without hindrance from the aforesaid abbot and convent or their successors. As for the dam in the monastery’s stream, I declare that Ludwig and his successors shall repair it at their own expense so that water may flow to their fishpond, but they must not raise the dam or make it higher than it is now. As for the ditch between Ludwig’s meadows and pastures and the holdings of those monastery people, we declare that the monastery people shall repair it one year when it is damaged, and Ludwig and his successors the next year, and so in turn for all future years whenever repair is needed. Both parties named above have promised on their own behalf and that of their successors faithfully and truly to observe and keep this settlement without any breach. As evidence, we have ordered our great seal, with our consent and certain knowledge, to be attached to this letter. Given and written at Krumau in the year after the birth of God’s Son 1465, on the Sunday of Saint Mauritius. The larger seal of Johann von Rosenberg, already described, hangs from a parchment strip in red wax.
